green roof.claim: Extensive and intensive green roofs can reduce runoff by 60 to 100 percent, respectively.
green roof.citation: U.S. EPA, 2025, Using Green Roofs to Reduce Heat Islands
green roof.note: The source reports runoff percentage, not the game's mm of reduced peak surface ponding; not directly comparable.
green roof.consistency_reason: The game value is 5 mm and has no event depth or roof design basis for conversion to percent runoff.

green roof.claim: The surface temperature of green roofs can be 56°F lower than those of conventional roofs.
green roof.citation: U.S. EPA, 2025, Using Green Roofs to Reduce Heat Islands
green roof.note: This is roof surface temperature and the game uses °C reduction at the hottest hard surface; the units and measured surfaces differ.
green roof.consistency_reason: 56°F is about 31.1°C, greater than the game's 1.6°C estimate, though the source and game contexts are not identical.

street tree + permeatable pavement + bio.claim: On average, urban forests were 3.0°F (1.6°C) cooler than urban non-green areas.
street tree + permeatable pavement + bio.citation: U.S. EPA, 2026, Benefits of Trees and Vegetation
street tree + permeatable pavement + bio.note: This supports the tree component but reports an urban-forest average, not the game's peak hard-surface temperature reduction; not directly comparable.
street tree + permeatable pavement + bio.consistency_reason: The source's 1.6°C average is below the game's 4.3°C estimate, and the source measures urban forests rather than one sidewalk intervention.
